definition: Prepossessing means creating a favorable impression — attractive or appealing in appearance or manner, especially at first sight.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word prepossessing. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know prepossessing should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The bakery's prepossessing window display, with its rows of glossy fruit tarts, drew customers inside before they had read a single review.
Pleasant describes anything mildly agreeable; prepossessing is stronger, suggesting looks or manner that actively win people over the moment they meet you.
Captivating goes further than prepossessing — it means holding someone completely spellbound, not just making a good first impression.

Appealing means attractive and pleasing — an appealing menu, an appealing offer. It is the broad, all-purpose word and says nothing about when the attraction strikes. Prepossessing is specifically about the first encounter: a face, manner, or display that creates a favorable impression on sight, before you know anything more.

Charming means delighting people through grace and winning manner — a charming host keeps guests smiling all evening. Charm can work slowly and keep working. Prepossessing does its work up front: it names the quality that disposes people in your favor the moment they meet you, whatever comes after.

Engaging means holding your attention and goodwill once you are involved — an engaging lecture keeps you listening. It describes the grip something has on you during the experience. Prepossessing acts earlier, winning favor at first sight, before any real involvement begins.

Prepossessing most often describes a person's appearance or manner, frequently in the phrases 'a prepossessing manner' or, in the negative, 'not very prepossessing.' It is about first impressions — use it when someone or something wins favor on sight, not after long acquaintance.

The cottage was the most prepossessing house the couple toured that spring: fresh paint, roses at the gate, windows that caught the afternoon light.
They made an offer the same evening, before the inspection report came back.
The report was sobering — damp in the cellar, wiring older than the roses, a chimney leaning a degree further each winter.
None of it had been visible from the front walk, and none of it changed how the house looked from the street.
They bought it anyway, joking later that they had been won over at the gate, and that everything after the gate was negotiation.
